chunks: And this hadith has been narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever listens intently to a letter from the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, without himself reciting, God will write for him a good deed, erase an evil deed from him, and raise him a level. Whoever recites it looking (from the text) without a voice, God will write for him, for every letter, a good deed, erase an evil deed from him, and raise him a level. Whoever learns a letter from it openly (by heart), God will write for him ten good deeds, erase ten evil deeds from him, and raise him ten levels.
He said: I do not say for every verse, but for every letter — 'Ba', or 'Ta', or the likes of these two.

He said: And whoever recites a letter clearly while seated in his salat, God will write for him, because of it, fifty good deeds, erase fifty evil deeds from him, and raise him fifty levels. And whoever recites a letter while standing in his salat, God will write for him, for every letter, one hundred good deeds, erase one hundred evil deeds from him, and raise him one hundred levels.
And whoever completes it (the Quran), there will be for him an answered supplication — either deferred or hastened.
He (the narrator) said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you — completing all of it?' He said: 'Completing all of it.'

key_terms.حَرْف: Letter (of the Arabic alphabet); the basic unit of Quranic reward in this hadith — not the verse (ayah)
key_terms.حَسَنَة: Good deed/merit — a unit of divine reward recorded in one's spiritual account
key_terms.خَتَمَ: To complete/seal the recitation of the entire Quran (khatam al-Quran)
key_terms.دَرَجَة: Level or rank in paradise — elevated through Quranic recitation
key_terms.دَعْوَة مُسْتَجَابَة: Answered supplication — promised to one who completes the Quran
key_terms.سَيِّئَة: Evil deed/sin — expiated through Quranic engagement

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting and listening to the Quran according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), narrating a hadith originally attributed to Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him), outlines a graduated scale of divine rewards for different modes of engaging with the Quran: listening without reciting earns one reward per letter, silent reading earns one per letter, memorization earns ten per letter, reciting while seated in prayer earns fifty per letter, and reciting while standing in prayer earns one hundred per letter. The hadith concludes with the promise of an answered supplication for completing the entire Quran. This teaching encouraged early Muslims to engage with the Quran in all available ways, even when full recitation was not possible, and emphasized that the reward is per letter — not per verse — making every individual sound of the Quran spiritually significant.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Mansour, from Muhammad Bin Bashir, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘And this Hadeeth has been reported from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

The one who listens intently to a letter from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic from without a recitation, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him a good deed and Delete an evil deed from him, and Raise a Level for him. 
And the one who recites looking from without a voice, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Write for him, for every letter, a good deed and Delete from him an evil deed, and Raise a Level for him; and the one who learns a letter from it apparently, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Write for him ten good deeds and Deleted ten evil deeds from him, and Raise ten Levels for him’.
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘I am not saying, for every Verse, but I am saying, for every letter, ‘B’, or ‘T’, or the likes of these two’.

Heasws said: ‘And the one who recites a Letter apparently while he is seated during his Salāt, Allahazwj would Write for him, due to it, fifty good deeds, and Delete fifty evil deeds from him, and Raise fifty Levels for him; and the one who recites a letter while he is standing during his Salāt, Allahazwj would Write for him, for every letter, one hundred good deeds, and Delete one hundred evil deeds from him, and Rasie one hundred Levels for him.
And the one who completes it, would be an Answered supplication for him, whether delared or hastened’.
I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! Completing all of it?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Completing all of it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from Ali ibn Hadid from Mansur from Muhammad ibn Bashir - who has narrated such Hadith from abu ‘Abd Allah  (a.s.) also from Ali ibn al- Husayn  (a.s.) who has said the following:

“If one listens to the reading of one letter from the book of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, without reading, Allah writes for him the reward for one good deed, deletes one of his evil deeds and raises for him one degree. If one reads looking but without audible voice Allah writes for him the reward for one good deed for each letter, deletes one of his evil deeds and raises him one degree. If one leams one clear letter Allah writes for him the reward for ten good deeds, deletes his ten evil deeds and raises him ten degrees.
The Imam said, ‘I do not say, ‘for every verse.’ I say for every letter. ‘B’, ‘T’ and so forth are letters.’

The Imam said, ‘If one reads one clear letter in prayer in a sitting position Allah writes for him the reward for fifty good deeds, deletes fifty of his evil deeds and raises for him fifty degrees. If one reads one letter in prayer standing, Allah, for each letter, writes for him the reward for one hundred good deeds, deletes one hundred of his evil deeds and raises him one hundred degrees.
If one completes reading the Holy Quran, for him there is an accepted prayer, sooner or later.’
“I (the narrator) then said to the Imam, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, is it completing the whole of it’? The Imam said, ‘Yes, it is completing the whole of the Holy Quran.’”
